components.description: DocHop design, construction and verification, then evaluation results

nodes.name: Existing benchmarks evaluate charts and documents in isolation
nodes.description: Existing benchmarks evaluate chart and document understanding separately, overlooking the interplay where surrounding narrative provides definitions and constraints needed to interpret charts.

nodes.name: DocHop tests integrated chart-context reasoning
nodes.description: DocHop is a benchmark where the document narrative specifies multi-step compositional constraints while charts supply the numerical values, requiring multi-hop reasoning rather than single-hop lookup.

nodes.name: Semantic reference labels prevent chart-only lookup
nodes.description: Questions are grounded on a semantic reference label assigned in the narrative rather than explicit entity names, so models must resolve target entities from the text before aggregating chart values.

nodes.name: Logic-first stochastic generation
nodes.description: Each instance starts from a sampled reasoning trace (a chain of conditional checks across charts); an LLM then generates the numerical data and document text to satisfy the trace, allowing control of reasoning depth D in {2,3,4,5} and chart count k in {2,3,4,6}.

nodes.name: Benchmark scale and diversity
nodes.description: DocHop has 2,074 examples across 6 task categories, 41 question templates, 480 topics and 7 chart types.

nodes.name: Multi-stage quality verification
nodes.description: Quality is ensured by programmatically executing each trace against data tables to verify answers, human verification of the narrative, and manual inspection of rendered images.

nodes.name: Models far below human accuracy
nodes.description: Human annotators exceed 90% accuracy while the best model, GPT-5.2 Reasoning, reaches only 62.83% overall (Table 1).

nodes.name: Reasoning variants outperform base models
nodes.description: Reasoning-enhanced variants outperform base counterparts, e.g. GPT-5.2 improves from 40.36% to 62.83% and Gemini-2.5-Flash from 24.88% to 32.02% (Table 1).

nodes.name: Accuracy degrades with depth and chart count
nodes.description: Accuracy of GPT-5.2 Reasoning and Gemini-2.5-Pro Reasoning decreases steadily as reasoning depth and number of charts increase, highest at k=2 and D=2 (Fig 5).

nodes.name: Human solving takes about five minutes
nodes.description: Human annotators need roughly five minutes per question, indicating DocHop requires careful multi-step reasoning rather than quick lookup.

nodes.name: Error modes: wrong entity, global max, OCR
nodes.description: Failure examples include attributing chart values to the wrong entity, taking the global maximum instead of the labeled entity set, and OCR errors in value extraction (Fig 4).

structural_reasoning: Benchmark motivation and design lead to verified dataset construction and then findings on model-human gap, reasoning and complexity.
